question: Is a decision its own fact, or part of ThreadResolved?

options.label: Two events
options.summary: The thread is resolved in one event and the decision is recorded in a second. A thread can close without a decision.
options.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as Person
  participant A as API
  participant L as Event log
  participant D as Decision log
  P->>A: ResolveThread(thread-7, "wrapper")
  A->>L: ThreadResolved
  A->>L: DecisionRecorded
  L->>D: project decision

axes.mechanical: 2 mechanical, 2 judgement (what a decision-less close means in the UI)
axes.silent: Decision log can lag the thread by one event
axes.invariant: "A decision references exactly one thread" stays a type; "every resolved thread has a decision" becomes a check

options.label: One event
options.summary: The resolve event carries the decision. A thread cannot close without one.
options.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as Person
  participant A as API
  participant L as Event log
  participant D as Decision log
  P->>A: ResolveThread(thread-7, "wrapper")
  A->>L: ThreadResolved{decision}
  L->>D: project decision

axes.invariant: Both invariants are types. Loses "close without deciding", which the domain vocabulary does not have

options.label: ThreadClosed, no decision
options.summary: The thread closes and nothing is recorded. This is what the first pass wrote.
options.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as Person
  participant A as API
  participant L as Event log
  P->>A: ResolveThread(thread-7)
  A->>L: ThreadClosed

axes.invariant: Breaks the domain vocabulary: there is no ThreadClosed

steps.caption: Pratos resolves thread 7 with one command and gives the decision in their own words.
The log records that the thread is resolved.
The log records who decided and what they chose. This second event can be left out.
The decision log is built from both events.
One event records that the thread is resolved and what was decided. Without a decision there is no resolve.
The decision log is built from that one event.
Every test passes, and the word ThreadClosed is not in the domain vocabulary.
